name: Modern Python typing (Protocols, TypedDict, PEP 695)
short_definition: 2026 default static typing style for Python ≥3.12: PEP 695 type-parameter syntax and type aliases, structural Protocols, TypedDict for JSON-shaped dicts, builtins list/dict/| unions, and boundary validation with Pydantic — checked by basedpyright in CI (ty optional in editor), not mypy-first greenfield.
scope_in: PEP 695 generics/aliases; Protocol vs ABC; TypedDict/NotRequired/ReadOnly/Unpack; type vs TypeAlias; never Any policy; cast/assert_type discipline; py.typed; gradual typing for legacy; interop with Pydantic models; mapping to TS interfaces/Zod at boundaries.
scope_out: Full basedpyright config matrix (py-typecheck); Pydantic v2 deep dive (py-pydantic-v2); runtime performance of typing; mypy plugin ecosystem as default; type stubs authoring for third-party C extensions beyond consuming typeshed.
defaults: requires-python >=3.12. Prefer PEP 695: `def f[T](x: T) -> T`, `class Repo[T]:`, `type Result[T] = Ok[T] | Err`. Use `X | None` not Optional; `list[str]` not List. Protocols for duck-typed deps (repositories, clock, HTTP client ports). TypedDict for wire JSON dicts when not using Pydantic models; Pydantic BaseModel for validated API/domain boundaries. Avoid Any; use unknown-equivalent patterns: object + narrow, TypeVar, or Protocol. New TypeVar/Generic[] only when supporting <3.12 (don't). Export public types from package; ship py.typed. CI: basedpyright (strict-ish); editor: basedpyright or ty for speed. Align mental model with typescript.md: domain types vs DTOs; validate at edges.
decision_gates: USE Protocol: interchangeable implementations, test fakes, hex ports. USE TypedDict: closed JSON objects without full validation yet / kwargs typing with Unpack. USE Pydantic: external input, settings, serialization. USE ABC: true shared implementation hierarchy needing isinstance registration. USE PEP 695 aliases for unions/results reused widely. DO NOT Protocol everything that should be a concrete dataclass. DO NOT TypedDict when you need runtime validation — use Pydantic. DO NOT mypy as greenfield default if basedpyright/ty stack chosen.
do_dont: DO: annotate public functions; PEP 695 generics; Protocol for IO ports; TypedDict total=False/NotRequired carefully; type aliases for Result-like unions; py.typed. DON'T: from typing import List, Dict, Optional (unless <3.9 — not our pin); bare Any to silence; type: ignore without code; cast without comment; mutable class vars without ClassVar; leak ORM models as API types; hand-sync TS interfaces to Python without codegen/contract.
failure_modes: 1) Any contagion silences real bugs. 2) Protocol mismatch only at typecheck — runtime still fails if not tested. 3) TypedDict total defaults surprise (missing keys). 4) PEP 695 syntax breaks if someone runs 3.11. 5) Circular imports from typing-only modules without TYPE_CHECKING / future annotations. 6) Pydantic model vs TypedDict drift. 7) Invariant list mutation errors misunderstood → incorrect cast.
anti_patterns: Agents must not: emit untyped public APIs; use List/Dict/Optional under 3.12+; default to Any; use TypeVar('T') boilerplate when PEP 695 works; # type: ignore without reason; isinstance hell instead of Protocol where structural fit; duplicate DTO fields in 5 modules; treat typing as optional in services.
tools: Primary: basedpyright (CI), ty (editor optional, Astral), ruff (UP rules pyupgrade-style), typing/typing_extensions only when backport needed (avoid if ≥3.12). Alternatives: mypy (legacy/brownfield with heavy plugin needs), pyright stock. Runtime: Pydantic v2 for validation.
versions_as_of: as_of 2026-07-13: Python 3.12–3.14 supported; PEP 695 since 3.12; basedpyright 1.39.9; ty 0.0.58 (pre-1.0 — editor assist, not sole CI gate yet); ruff 0.15.x with pyupgrade/UP rules. Prefer language features from stdlib typing docs current 3.x.
config_snippets:
# pyproject.toml
[project]
requires-python = ">=3.12"

[tool.basedpyright]
include = ["src"]
typeCheckingMode = "standard"  # or strict when ready
reportAny = "warning"
reportUnknownParameterType = "warning"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "ANN"]  # ANN optional if basedpyright owns annotations

# CI
# uv run basedpyright
# uv run ruff check
deprecation_watch: typing.List/Dict/Optional/Tuple in new code; TypeVar+Generic boilerplate for 3.12+; mypy as default greenfield; typing_extensions for features already in 3.12; comment-based type hints; untyped **kwargs without TypedDict Unpack.
ts_boundary: Map conceptually: Protocol ≈ interface; TypedDict ≈ type shape for JSON; Pydantic ≈ Zod at runtime. Contract-first OpenAPI generates TS types (typescript.md) — do not hand-sync. Domain vs DTO split mirrors TS guidance. Prefer Result unions similar to TS Result<T>.
rust_boundary: Rust enums/Result are stronger; Python uses unions + conventions. When correctness-critical parsers needed, implement in Rust and expose via API — don't over-type fragile Python. Shared schema still OpenAPI/protobuf.
supabase_boundary: DB rows: TypedDict or Pydantic models matching generated schema; never trust PostgREST JSON without validation at boundary. Keep snake_case DTOs at DB edge; map to domain types inside service (same as TS domain vs DTO rule).
boundary_contracts: OpenAPI schemas ↔ Pydantic models source of truth for HTTP; JSON Schema for events; env via pydantic-settings typed model. MCP tool args: explicit TypedDict or Pydantic, never dict[str, Any].
decision_matrix_row: Problem: structural ports/fakes → Python Protocol. Problem: validated HTTP body → Pydantic (Python) / Zod (TS). Problem: closed JSON dict typing without validators → TypedDict. Problem: max memory-safety parser → Rust. Problem: UI state types → TypeScript only.
threats: Type holes (Any, unchecked cast) give false security; confused deputies via structurally typed Protocols accepting malicious objects if runtime not validated; desync between types and runtime validation enabling injection at edges.
mitigations: Validate all external input at runtime (Pydantic); forbid bare Any in public APIs via checker settings; no cast on untrusted data; CI typecheck gate; pair Protocols with tests on real implementations.
agent_codegen_policy: MUST: annotate public functions/methods; use PEP 695 and | unions; Protocol for ports; TypedDict or Pydantic for wire data; py.typed on packages. MUST NOT: Any to silence; List/Dict/Optional imports; untyped **kwargs; type: ignore without code; skip basedpyright in service templates.
tests_required: Typecheck in CI (basedpyright). Unit tests for runtime validation paths (Pydantic). Protocol fakes in tests must match Protocol. Optional: typing pytest plugins not required if checker is strict.
ci_gates: basedpyright clean (or agreed severity); ruff UP for modern syntax; no new type: ignore without review label.
skill_scan_signals: POSITIVE: PEP 695 syntax, Protocol ports, TypedDict/Pydantic DTOs, py.typed, | None, basedpyright config. NEGATIVE: rampant Any; typing.List; untyped public API; only runtime without types; mypy.ini without basedpyright in new repos; # type: ignore sprawl.
skill_module_bullets:
- Python ≥3.12: PEP 695 generics/aliases; list/dict/X|Y builtins; no typing.List/Optional in new code.
- Protocol for ports; TypedDict for JSON shapes; Pydantic for validated boundaries.
- Domain types vs DTOs (mirror TS module); map at edges.
- CI basedpyright; ty optional editor; mypy not greenfield default.
- py.typed on libraries; ban Any in public APIs.
action_items: 1) Typing section in references/python.md. 2) basedpyright defaults in template pyproject. 3) Scan rules for typing.List/Any/public untyped defs. 4) Examples Protocol+TypedDict+PEP695. 5) Cross-link py-typecheck and py-pydantic-v2.

conflicts_noted: ty is fast but pre-1.0 (0.0.x as of research) — keep basedpyright as CI source of truth until ty stable. mypy still better for some plugin ecosystems (Django) — brownfield exception. TypedDict vs Pydantic: teams disagree; policy is Pydantic at trust boundaries, TypedDict for lightweight internal shapes.
